what_it_shows: Front view of Air Canada 767 C-GAUN at rest on the Gimli runway right after the landing: nose gear collapsed so the nose sits on the concrete, people and a truck around it, a metal guardrail running down the runway centre in the foreground, and a red VW Beetle parked at left. 728x505, colour, 1983. The single best 'proof' frame: real jet, real runway, a car next to it.
best_segments: Full frame is landscape; for 9:16 use a 284x505 crop centred on the nose (x 213-497) for the hook, then pull out/pan left to reveal the red Beetle (x 0-284) on the 'drag strip' line. Low-res: keep scale <=1.5x, add slight grain rather than upscaling hard. Must credit + keep CC BY-SA on the derivative frame.

license: Public domain as tagged on Commons ({{PD-USGov-FAA}}, sourced from FAA Lessons Learned). CAUTION: provenance is weak - an FAA employee is unlikely to have shot a Canadian accident scene in 1983; the original photographer is not named. Treat as unverified PD; prefer the CC BY-SA front photo.
credit_line: Photo: FAA Lessons Learned / Wikimedia Commons (public domain as tagged)
what_it_shows: Black-and-white side view of C-GAUN on the Gimli runway: nose down on the concrete, tail high, rear evacuation slides deployed, a few people beside the engines, guardrail in the foreground. 612x501.
best_segments: Use only if rights are accepted: crop the slides + nose-down attitude (x 150-612) for the 'everyone got out' beat. Very low-res.

kind: photo (the actual aircraft, C-GAUN, back in service)
credit_line: Photo: Andrew Thomas (Shrewsbury, UK) via Flickr / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0
what_it_shows: C-GAUN, fin 604, in the 1980s Air Canada livery (red-orange cheatline, maple-leaf tail) taxiing at Toronto Pearson on 14 Jul 1984, one year after Gimli. 3835x2363 film scan - same era livery as the accident.
best_segments: Hook shot ('This jet...'): 9:16 window 1329x2363 panning left-to-right from the tail (x ~1000) to the AIR CANADA titles/nose (x ~2600). Sharp enough for a slow 1.2x push-in.

credit_line: Photo: Aero Icarus (Zurich) via Flickr / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0
what_it_shows: C-GAUN in the 1990s green-tail Air Canada livery taxiing at Miami, 24 Jan 1998. 4866x3222, the highest-res frame of the real jet. Later livery than 1983.
best_segments: Large enough for a 9:16 crop at full height (1812x3222) on the nose/engine (x ~0-1812) or a slow lateral pan along the fuselage; good for the 'pounds vs kilograms' overlay background.

credit_line: Photo: Ikluft / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0
what_it_shows: The 'Gimli Glider' parked in retirement at Mojave Air & Space Port, 12 Feb 2008, desert and snow-capped mountains behind. 3072x2048.
best_segments: Optional outro/'where is it now' beat; 9:16 crop 1152x2048 around x 400-1552 (mid-fuselage + wing).

what_it_shows: Scanned colour print: a motorcycle (described as Cory Gurman on a 1982 Kawasaki GPZ1100) racing down the old concrete Gimli runway, a guardrail and spectators/parked cars along the side. Uploaded 2015, EXIF date flagged invalid; looks like a 1980s print, but the exact year is NOT documented - do not caption it as 1983.
best_segments: The 'runway turned drag strip' beat: 9:16 crop 1669x2967 centred on the bike and guardrail (x ~1500-3169). Faded colours match the 1983 footage tone.

credit_line: Photo: Vince Pahkala / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0
what_it_shows: Two drag cars (red Camaro-style car in front) at the start line of Interlake Dragway at Gimli, 29 Jun 2013, timing tower and spectators behind. Sponsor signs (CHUDDS, Motion, Interlake Dragway) are visible - trademarks, crop or blur if they distract.
best_segments: Quick 1-second insert for 'drag strip': 9:16 crop 801x1424 on the red car (x ~100-901), which keeps most sponsor boards out.

credit_line: Lockwood, G.H., Final Report of the Board of Inquiry ... Air Canada Boeing 767 C-GAUN ... Gimli, Manitoba, 23 July 1983 (April 1985)
what_it_shows: 208-page scanned final report by Mr. Justice George H. Lockwood. Key pages (PDF page numbers): p15 crew/passenger count; p34-35 conversion-factor error, 41,000 ft, engine failures, glider skill, side-slip, drag strip; p43 1.77 vs .8 factors; p47-48 step-by-step fuel miscalculation.
best_segments: Reference only. If permission is ever obtained, PDF p48 (the four-step wrong vs correct fuel calculation) is the best on-screen 'receipt'. Otherwise rebuild the numbers as an original Curio diagram.
